body.p: Claims 1-26 were previously pending with Claims 1, 12, and 23 being independent. Claims 1-5, 7-16, 18-20, and 22-23 have been amended herein. Support for the amendments can be found at the least at [0040] - [0044], [0048], [0050], and FIGS. 2-6. No new matter is added. Accordingly, Claims 1-26 are pending, with claims 1, 12, and 23 being independent. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application, in light of the above amendments and the present remarks.

An interview was held on October 28, 2024, between Examiner McCrosky and Nathanial Smith (Reg. No. 78,807). Proposed claim amendments and the cited art were discussed. Examineragreed that the proposed amendments overcome the currently cited art and that more search and consideration would be required. Applicant appreciates the Examiner's time and consideration extended for the interview.
35 U.S.C. Q 103 Rejections

Claims 1-5, 7, 12-16, and 23-25 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2006/0247508 to Fennell (hereinafter "Fennell") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0245910 to Mallas et al. (hereinafter "Mallas") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0167,167 to Mitchell (hereinafter "Mitchell") and in further view of U.S. Patent No. 5,800,420 to Gross et al., (hereinafter "Gross"). Claims 6 and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell in view of Gross and in further view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2002/0042561 to Schulman et al. ("Schulman"). Claims 8-11, 19-22, and 26 stand rejected as allegedly being obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell in view of Gross and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0270,617 to Muller ("Muller"). As a primafacie case of the obviousness of claims 1-26 cannot be established based upon the asserted combination of references, Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections as set forth below.
1. The cited art does not teach the instant claims.
Gross is referenced to allegedly teach three separate power sources. Office Action, p. 6. Gross describes an analyte controlled liquid delivery system. The liquid delivery system comprises

a needle that penetrates the skin of a user and delivers insulin to the user. Gross, Abstract. Gross generally describes a power source, which may be a battery, and "one or more power sources (not shown)." Gross, 17:28-31, (emphasis added). The Examiner references Gross at Col. 17, lines 31- 33. The "one or more power sources" that the Examiner is referencing do not provide power to electrodes. Furthermore, these "one or more power sources" are not independently providing power to independent electrodes. There is no description in Gross of how the voltages are distributed to the electrodes except from a single power source. So, though a plurality of power sources may be generally disclosed in Gross, there is no description of how those power sources are instructed or how those power sources are used to supply voltage to the various electrodes.

As such, Gross combined with the cited art may capture a plurality of power sources; however, a controller providing independent instruction to three power sources is not disclosed. Providing three independent voltages to the electrodes based on the independent instructions is also not disclosed. Furthermore, any structure of an operational circuit comprising three distinct voltage sources is not disclosed. Any modification of the current art to disclose an operational circuit including a plurality of power sources providing separate voltages to the electrodes is left to the imagination as the circuit components are not disclosed. As such, no combination of any elements of the currently cited art provides a complete operational circuit comprising three distinct voltage sources each voltage source operational to receive instructions and generate independent voltages to each electrode. As such, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejections are deficient and hereby requests corresponding Notice of Allowance or a new Non-Final Office Action correcting these deficiencies.

To advance prosecution, the claims have been amended to clarify the distinctions between the claims and the cited art. Specifically, exemplary claim 1 has been amended to recite subject matter directed to instructing each distinct power source independently and providing independent voltages to each electrode. As described above, this is not disclosed in the cited art. Therefore, there is no teaching in Gross or any combination of the cited art providing three instructions to three independent voltage sources and providing three independent voltages to the three electrodes. Simply stating that the power source could be multiple power sources combined with the structure and function of the currently cited art does not teach the instant claims.
2. It would not be obvious to modify the art to teach the instant claims.

Simply stating that a voltage source could be a plurality of voltage sources does not provide the necessary controller instructions, the necessary electronic components, or the necessary three- independent-voltage source diagram or description necessary to complete the circuit using three independent voltage sources. As such, all components necessary to teach the instant claims are not provided or arranged to provide an operational circuit including three independent voltage sources. As such, undue experimentation and modification would be required to modify at least Fennell and Mallas as described below.

It would not be obvious to modify Fennell to teach the instant claims. Fennell describes signaling a singular voltage source used to provide voltage to the working electrode, and guard electrode. Fennell describes the power source as coupled to an operational amplifier to provide different voltages to each of these elements. Fennell at [0032]-[0034]. Specifically, Fennell discloses, "the work electrode 210 is operatively coupled to the inverting input terminal 404 of the operational amplifier 402, while the guard electrode 211 is operatively coupled to the non- inverting input terminal 405 of the operational amplifier 402. It can be further seen that the work voltage source Vw is provided to the non-inverting terminal 405." Fennell at [0032]; FIG. 4A. Fennell requires that the guard electrode and working electrode maintain the same voltage. Fennell at [0032]. Fennell is silent with respect to using separate voltage sources for the working electrode, the counter electrode, and the guard electrode. As such, the circuit of Fennell would have to be modified and tested providing components that do not currently exist in the circuit and omitting components that do currently exist to arrive at an operational circuit including three voltage sources. Simply adding the "one or more power sources" ... "(not shown)" of Gross does not lead to a complete operational circuit as described above. As such, undue experimentation and modification would be required.

Again, the circuit of Mallas would have to be modified and tested providing components that do not currently exist in the circuit and omitting components that do currently exist to arrive at an operational circuit including three voltage sources. Simply adding the "one or more power sources" ... "(not shown)" of Gross does not lead to a complete operational circuit as described above. As such, undue experimentation and modification would be required.
As such, Applicant submits that the current claims are not taught by any combination of the cited art and respectfully request withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections.
Dependent Claims

Applicant respectfully submits that those dependent claims not discussed separately herein are allowable at least for the reasons discussed with respect to the corresponding independent claims, and respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections thereof be withdrawn.

Applicant submits that claims 1-26, as amended, are in allowable condition and request a corresponding Notice of Allowance. In the event of any outstanding issues, Applicants respectfully request an Examiner Interview to expedite prosecution.
